title: Christian, recognize your dignity

cards: Same man, different day. Not on a road facing an invader this time, but in a church in Rome on Christmas, preaching to a crowd.
The sermon starts with joy: our Savior is born today, he tells them, so let us be glad, because there's no room for sadness on the birthday of Life.

Then, partway through, he turns and speaks to each listener directly, as if pointing at them. Christian, recognize your dignity. The line has traveled a long way; the Catechism of the Catholic Church quotes it today.

teach.b: Start with what comes before the line. Leo has been preaching that in the birth of Jesus, God took on our human nature, so that people could share in God's own life. That's the engine of the sermon.
Then comes the turn: Christian, recognize your dignity, and since you've been made a sharer in the divine nature, don't go back to your old meanness by the way you live. Next, the reminder.
Remember, Leo says, whose body you belong to, and who its head is. Remember that you were rescued from the power of darkness and brought into God's light and kingdom. Notice what he's doing.
He doesn't say: you are worthless, so try harder. He says the opposite. You have been given something enormous, so live like someone who has it.

The dignity comes first; the living follows from it. The Catechism places this line at the opening of its section on the Christian life. Before it talks about any commandment, it reminds the reader who they are.
Now the word itself. In the Acts of the Apostles, the disciples were first called Christians at Antioch.
For Leo's listeners, it was a name that tied them to Christ.
When he calls out Christian, he isn't scolding a crowd. He's naming them, and telling people their worth before telling them anything else.

how: Catholics hear Leo's Christmas sermon in the Office of Readings at Christmas, and the Catechism opens its section on life in Christ with his line about recognizing one's dignity.

games.q: you're Leo, preaching on Christmas. you want people to live better. how do you begin?
o: list their sins and warn them.
remind them who they are, then ask them to live like it.
tell them to try harder next year.
games.why: Leo names their dignity first, as sharers in the divine nature, and only then asks them not to go back to their old ways.

practice: Sit as if you were worth sitting well, feet flat, back long, shoulders down, and listen for the tone of the voice in your head that comments on your mistakes.
Then say one thing to yourself the way you'd speak to someone you respect: plainly, kindly, without flattery.
If you pray, hear Leo's line as spoken to you, Christian, recognize your dignity; if you don't, simply rest in the posture of someone who matters.

wordCard.voice: Christian. A follower of Christ, the name the disciples were first called at Antioch, and the name Leo used to call his listeners to their dignity. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: Christian, recognize your dignity — Leo's own words.
